ios.desc:
⏰ An alarm clock that knows how long your trip will take.

Most alarms wake you at a fixed time. Time To Go checks how long it takes to reach where you are going right now — with today's traffic and transit — and shows it the moment your alarm rings, so you know whether to get moving or you still have a few minutes.

SET A DESTINATION
Pick a place by searching for it, or save the ones you go to often. Your departure point can be your current location or any fixed address. Choose how you travel: transit, driving, or walking.

SEE YOUR TRAVEL TIME WHEN IT MATTERS
When the alarm goes off, the travel time to your destination and your estimated arrival are right there on screen. Open the route to see each leg of the trip — which bus, which line, how many minutes — refreshed live.

PREP TIME
Leaving right away, in 5 minutes, or in 10? Add prep time and the arrival estimate moves with it.

LOCK SCREEN ALARMS ON iOS 26
On iOS 26, alarms use the system alarm, so they ring through Silent mode and Focus and even when the app is closed — with your travel time on the lock screen.

EVERYTHING AN ALARM SHOULD DO
• Repeat on the days you choose
• Six alarm sounds, previewed before you pick
• Snooze
• Volume follows your device
• Dark mode
• Korean and English

Sign in with Apple or Google to keep your alarms and saved places when you change devices.

Travel times are estimates from map providers and can differ from actual conditions.

quotes.text:
I'm a first-time app developer from Seoul. Most alarms only tell you the
time, but the thing I actually needed to know every morning was whether
I could still make it — so this one checks the live transit/traffic
route to wherever you're headed at the moment it rings, and shows the
travel time and arrival on the lock screen.

On iOS 26 it uses AlarmKit, so it rings through Silent mode and Focus
and works with the app killed. That part was the hard bit: the system
owns the alarm UI completely, custom sounds have to be .caf in the
bundle, and dismissing your own screen doesn't stop the alarm — you
have to call stop() yourself.

What I can't do is test it outside Korea. I use Kakao's transit API here
and fall back to Google Directions elsewhere, and I have no idea how
good those results are in other cities. If you try it, I'd love to know
whether the travel time is anywhere near right for your commute.

Free, one banner ad, sign-in optional. iOS only.
